questions.text: With reference to the cultural history of India, consider the following statements regarding the 'Sarvodaya' movement: 1. The term 'Sarvodaya' was first coined by Mahatma Gandhi as the title of his translation of John Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'. 2. Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan Movement was a direct offshoot of the Sarvodaya philosophy. 3. Jayaprakash Narayan's 'Total Revolution' in the 1970s was explicitly based on Sarvodaya principles. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use 'Person-Idea Association' verification. Statement 1: Gandhi coined 'Sarvodaya' (Welfare of All) for his 1908 Gujarati translation of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' (Correct). Statement 2: Vinoba Bhave is the quintessential Sarvodaya leader; Bhoodan (Gift of Land) was the practical application of Sarvodaya (Correct). Statement 3: JP Narayan's 'Total Revolution' (1974) was deeply rooted in Gandhian Sarvodaya ideals of non-violent societal reconstruction (Correct). All three statements are factually accurate.

questions.text: As per the table below showing prevalence of Anaemia in women (aged 15-49 years) from NFHS-4 (2015-16) to NFHS-5 (2019-21), which state recorded the highest increase in percentage points?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Calculate simple difference (NFHS-5 minus NFHS-4) for each. Gujarat: 65 - 55 = +10. Kerala: 36 - 34 = +2. Bihar: 63 - 60 = +3. Madhya Pradesh: 54 - 52 = +2. Gujarat (+10) is the highest by a wide margin. Worked Solution: Percentage point change = NFHS-5 % - NFHS-4 %. Gujarat: 65 - 55 = 10 pp. Kerala: 36 - 34 = 2 pp. Bihar: 63 - 60 = 3 pp. Madhya Pradesh: 54 - 52 = 2 pp. Gujarat shows the maximum increase of 10 percentage points.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Unemployment Rate (Usual Status) by Education Level for persons aged 15 years and above as per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24, which education category exhibits the highest unemployment rate?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'Unemployment Rate %' column for the maximum value. Graduate & Above (13.4%) is the highest. General awareness shortcut: In India, unemployment rates typically rise with education levels (educated unemployment phenomenon). Step-by-step: 1) List the UR for each category: Not Literate (1.2%), Primary & Middle (2.1%), Secondary & Higher Secondary (4.8%), Diploma/Certificate (10.2%), Graduate & Above (13.4%). 2) Compare the percentages. 3) 13.4% > 10.2% > 4.8% > 2.1% > 1.2%. 4) Graduate & Above has the highest unemployment rate.

questions.text: Refer to the table below showing State-wise Installed Renewable Energy Capacity (Solar + Wind) in GW as on 31st March 2023 and 31st March 2024. Which state recorded the highest percentage growth in total renewable capacity during this period?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare (Increase/Base) ratios using approximation. Rajasthan: +6.0 on 21.5 (~28%). Gujarat: +5.5 on 20.0 (27.5%). Tamil Nadu: +2.0 on 16.5 (~12%). Karnataka: +2.0 on 13.5 (~15%). Rajasthan's ratio 6/21.5 > 5.5/20. Step-by-step: Total 2023: Raj 21.5, Guj 20.0, TN 16.5, Kar 13.5. Total 2024: Raj 27.5, Guj 25.5, TN 18.5, Kar 15.5. Growth %: Raj (6/21.5*100=27.9%), Guj (5.5/20*100=27.5%), TN (2/16.5*100=12.1%), Kar (2/13.5*100=14.8%). Rajasthan is highest.

questions.text: As per the data table below showing the sectoral contribution to India's Gross Value Added (GVA) at current prices for the financial year 2022-23 (First Revised Estimates), which sector had the highest percentage share?

options.label: C
options.text: C. Services (Trade, Hotels, Transport, Communication, Financial, Real Estate, Public Admin, Others)

options.label: D
options.text: D. Industry and Services had equal shares

questions.solution: Shortcut: In the Indian economy, the Services sector consistently contributes over 50% of GVA. Scan the 'Percentage Share' column for the highest value; it will be the Services row. Full Solution: The table shows Agriculture ~18.3%, Industry ~28.3%, and Services ~53.4%. The Services sector has the highest share, making Option C correct.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Major Deficit Indicators of the Central Government (as % of GDP) for Actuals 2022-23, Revised Estimates 2023-24, and Budget Estimates 2024-25, which deficit indicator recorded the largest absolute decline (in percentage points) from Actual 2022-23 to Budget Estimates 2024-25?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compute the drop (Actual 2022-23 minus BE 2024-25) for each deficit mentally: Fiscal Deficit drops 6.4 - 4.9 = 1.5 pp; Revenue Deficit drops 3.9 - 1.8 = 2.1 pp; Primary Deficit drops 2.6 - 1.5 = 1.1 pp; Effective Revenue Deficit drops 2.8 - 1.1 = 1.7 pp. The largest drop is 2.1 pp for Revenue Deficit. Step-by-step: 1) Identify Actual 2022-23 and BE 2024-25 columns. 2) Subtract BE 2024-25 value from Actual 2022-23 value for each row. 3) Fiscal: 6.4 - 4.9 = 1.5. Revenue: 3.9 - 1.8 = 2.1. Primary: 2.6 - 1.5 = 1.1. Effective Revenue: 2.8 - 1.1 = 1.7. 4) Compare differences: 2.1 > 1.7 > 1.5 > 1.1. 5) Revenue Deficit has the highest decline.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Budget Estimates (BE) for Major Subsidies (in ₹ Lakh Crore) for FY 2024-25, the allocation for Food Subsidy is approximately what percentage of the total subsidy allocation (Food + Fertilizer + Petroleum)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Approximate Total = 2.05 + 1.64 + 0.01 = 3.70. Food % = 2.05/3.70. Use fraction 20.5/37. 37*0.5 = 18.5. 37*0.55 = 20.35. 20.5 is closest to 20.35, so ~55%. Step-by-step: Total Subsidy BE 2024-25 = 2.05 (Food) + 1.64 (Fertilizer) + 0.01 (Petroleum) = 3.70 Lakh Crore. Food Share = (2.05 / 3.70) * 100 = 55.4%. Option C (55%) is the closest approximation.

questions.text: Refer to the table below showing Forest Cover in major states (in sq km) as per India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2019 and 2021. Which state recorded a decline in forest cover between the two assessment periods?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Compare the two columns vertically; look for the only row where the 2021 figure is less than the 2019 figure. Madhya Pradesh: 77,493 > 77,482 (Increase). Arunachal Pradesh: 66,431 < 66,688 (Decrease). Chhattisgarh: 55,717 > 55,611 (Increase). Odisha: 52,156 > 51,619 (Increase). Only Arunachal Pradesh shows a decline. Worked Solution: Subtract 2019 value from 2021 value for each option. MP: +11. Arunachal: -257. Chhattisgarh: +106. Odisha: +537. Negative change indicates decline. Arunachal Pradesh is the correct answer.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Quarter-wise GVA Growth Rates (YoY %) at Constant Prices for major sectors in FY 2023-24, which sector witnessed the highest increase in growth rate (in percentage points) from Q1 to Q2?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'Change (Q2-Q1)' column mentally. Agriculture & Services show negative change (decline). Construction rises by ~2.6 pts. Manufacturing jumps from 4.7% to 13.2%, a rise of 8.5 pts – the highest by inspection. Step-by-step: Calculate Q2 minus Q1 for each: Agri (1.2-3.5=-2.3), Mfg (13.2-4.7=8.5), Serv (5.8-10.3=-4.5), Const (10.5-7.9=2.6). Manufacturing has the highest positive difference.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Year-on-Year (YoY) growth in Outstanding Bank Credit deployed across major sectors (Provisional data, March 2024), which sector recorded the lowest growth rate?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'YoY Growth %' column for the smallest number. Industry (8.4%) is visibly lower than Agriculture (18.1%), Services (15.2%), and Personal Loans (17.8%). No calculation needed, just vertical comparison. Step-by-step: 1) Read the growth percentage for each sector from the table. 2) Agriculture: 18.1%. Industry: 8.4%. Services: 15.2%. Personal Loans: 17.8%. 3) Compare the four values. 4) 8.4% is the minimum. 5) Therefore, Industry sector recorded the lowest YoY credit growth.

questions.text: Refer to the table below listing major Tiger Reserves, their States, and the estimated Tiger Population as per the 2022 cycle of the All India Tiger Estimation. Which reserve recorded the second-highest tiger population?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the top two values in the 'Tiger Population' column. Corbett (260) is clearly the highest. Scan the remaining rows for the next highest number; Bandipur (150) is higher than Nagarhole (141) and Bandhavgarh (135). Full Solution: Sorting the population column descending: Corbett (260), Bandipur (150), Nagarhole (141), Bandhavgarh (135). Bandipur is second highest.

questions.text: As per the table below showing the Gross Value Added (GVA) growth rates at Constant (2011-12) Prices for major sectors (Provisional Estimates 2021-22 and First Revised Estimates 2022-23), which sector witnessed the largest decline in growth rate (in percentage points) between the two years?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Scan the 'Change' mentally (2022-23 minus 2021-22). Agriculture: 4.0 - 3.5 = +0.5. Industry: 4.4 - 11.6 = -7.2. Services: 9.5 - 8.8 = +0.7. Construction (sub-component of Industry): 9.0 - 14.8 = -5.8. Industry has the largest negative swing (-7.2 pp). Worked Solution: Calculate the difference for each option. Agri: +0.5 pp. Industry: 4.4 - 11.6 = -7.2 pp. Services: +0.7 pp. Construction: 9.0 - 14.8 = -5.8 pp. The most negative value (largest decline) is Industry at -7.2 percentage points.

questions.text: The table below shows the chronological order of key events during the Indian National Movement. Which of the following sequences represents the correct chronological order (Earliest to Latest)?

options.label: A
options.text: A. Champaran Satyagraha → Jallianwala Bagh Massacre → Non-Cooperation Movement → Dandi March

options.label: B
options.text: B. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre → Champaran Satyagraha → Dandi March → Non-Cooperation Movement

options.label: C
options.text: C. Champaran Satyagraha → Non-Cooperation Movement → Jallianwala Bagh Massacre → Dandi March

options.label: D
options.text: D. Non-Cooperation Movement → Champaran Satyagraha → Jallianwala Bagh Massacre → Dandi March

questions.solution: Shortcut: Anchor the earliest event. Champaran (1917) is Gandhi's first major Satyagraha in India. Jallianwala Bagh (1919) follows. Non-Cooperation (1920-22) follows Jallianwala. Dandi March (1930) is much later. Only Option A follows this anchor sequence. Full Solution: Dates: Champaran (1917), Jallianwala Bagh (1919), Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Dandi March (1930). Option A matches this order perfectly.

questions.text: As per the table below showing Population and Area data for selected states (Census 2011), which state has the highest Population Density (persons per sq km)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Approximate Density = Population / Area. Bihar: 10.4 Cr / 0.94 Lakh ≈ 1106. West Bengal: 9.1 Cr / 0.89 Lakh ≈ 1022. Kerala: 3.3 Cr / 0.39 Lakh ≈ 846. Uttar Pradesh: 19.9 Cr / 2.41 Lakh ≈ 825. Bihar is clearly the highest. No exact division needed; ratio comparison suffices. Worked Solution: Calculate density for each. Bihar: 104,099,452 / 94,163 ≈ 1105. WB: 91,276,115 / 88,752 ≈ 1028. Kerala: 33,406,061 / 38,852 ≈ 860. UP: 199,812,341 / 240,928 ≈ 829. Bihar (1105) > WB (1028) > Kerala (860) > UP (829).

questions.text: Refer to the table below showing Budget Estimates (BE) 2023-24 vs Revised Estimates (RE) 2022-23 for key Central Government Schemes (in ₹ Crore). Which scheme received the highest percentage increase in allocation?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate decreases first. MGNREGA: 60,000 < 89,400 (Decrease). PM-KISAN: 60,000 = 60,000 (No change). Compare remaining two. JJM: Increase 10k on 60k base ≈ 16.6%. PMAY: Increase 31k on 48k base ≈ 64.5%. PMAY increase is roughly 4x JJM. Worked Solution: Calculate % change = (BE - RE)/RE * 100. MGNREGA: (60k-89.4k)/89.4k = -32.8%. PMAY: (79k-48k)/48k = 31/48 ≈ 64.6%. JJM: (70k-60k)/60k = 10/60 ≈ 16.7%. PM-KISAN: 0%. PMAY has the highest positive percentage increase.
